purpose: Individually authored episode questions and coverage boundaries for Computer & PC. The subject progression is organized by concrete content rather than a topic-by-angle multiplication.

categories.title: Reading the computer as a system

topics.question: What happens between pressing a PC's power button and seeing the login screen?
topics.coverage: Trace firmware, device initialization, boot selection and operating-system startup using vendor diagrams; distinguish stages without giving firmware-flashing instructions.

topics.question: How do CPU cores, clock speed and instruction behavior jointly affect work?
topics.coverage: Compare a documented processor workload with serial and parallel portions; reject rankings based on clock rate alone.

topics.question: Why do RAM capacity and storage capacity solve different problems?
topics.coverage: Follow a large working dataset through memory, paging and persistent files; use operating-system counters instead of treating free memory as the only performance measure.

topics.question: How does a motherboard determine which upgrades can actually work?
topics.coverage: Read socket, chipset, firmware, physical-clearance and memory-support documentation for a named board revision; avoid compatibility claims based only on matching connectors.

topics.question: Which PCIe lanes are available to a device on one motherboard?
topics.coverage: Map CPU and chipset lanes, link generation and shared slots using a named board manual, then test actual link width and workload rather than quote raw bandwidth alone.

categories.reading_subcategory: Reading the computer as a system

topics.question: Why can a CPU with more cores finish a particular task more slowly?
topics.coverage: Compare scheduling, thermal limits, per-core work and software scaling under controlled conditions; identify benchmark versions and avoid a universal brand verdict.

topics.question: How does integrated graphics share resources with the rest of a PC?
topics.coverage: Trace system memory, display outputs and power budgets using actual architecture documentation; distinguish graphics capability from discrete video-memory labels.

topics.question: What does GPU utilization fail to reveal about a rendering bottleneck?
topics.coverage: Compare compute activity, memory bandwidth, VRAM allocation, decoding and CPU feeding through a defined workload; do not infer capability from one dashboard percentage.

topics.question: Why do video-memory capacity and graphics speed need separate evaluation?
topics.coverage: Contrast a workload that fits in memory with one that spills or fails; include precision and software support instead of comparing gigabytes alone.

topics.question: What limited Pentium 4 NetBurst clock scaling, and what changed afterward?
topics.coverage: Compare dated processor models, thermal guidance, power and instructions per clock; avoid a false hard 4 GHz barrier or a single-cause account of Intel?s architecture shift.

topics.question: When does ray tracing improve a rendered scene enough to justify its PC cost?
topics.coverage: Compare the same game or renderer with rasterization and selected ray-traced effects, holding resolution, quality settings and hardware fixed.

topics.question: What did Apple?s first M1 Mac change about PC architecture comparisons?
topics.coverage: Compare a named 2020 M1 Mac with a contemporary x86 system for workload, power, integrated memory and software compatibility; avoid architecture-wide winner claims.

topics.question: Which workloads benefit from an AMD 3D V-Cache processor, and why?
topics.coverage: Compare named X3D and non-X3D models under matched memory, GPU and game settings; relate cache behavior to observed results without universal victory claims.

topics.question: When does an SSD interface become less important than its sustained workload behavior?
topics.coverage: Inspect latency, caching, temperature and steady-state writes from reproducible tests; keep SATA, PCIe generation and device controller behavior distinct.

topics.question: Why is a second partition on the same drive not an independent backup?
topics.coverage: Model device failure, deletion and recovery boundaries; consult backup documentation and demonstrate only with disposable files.

topics.question: How can a restore test reveal gaps in an apparently successful backup?
topics.coverage: Specify selected files, application state, encryption keys and recovery time; compare restored content against a known baseline without using private user data.

topics.question: What do drive-health indicators establish about future reliability?
topics.coverage: Read manufacturer definitions and error records; distinguish warning signals, uncertainty and recoverability without promising that any status predicts failure precisely.

topics.question: When does an SSD slow after its write cache fills?
topics.coverage: Test a named NAND type, controller, capacity and firmware across sustained writes and recovery time; distinguish SLC caching from intrinsic QLC speed.

topics.question: How can a cooling limit change a processor's sustained performance?
topics.coverage: Compare temperatures, clock behavior and power under a repeatable workload; use vendor operating limits and avoid encouraging thermal-protection bypasses.

topics.question: Why does a power supply's wattage label not establish its complete suitability?
topics.coverage: Examine connectors, documented protections, transient requirements and independent test methods; exclude opening power supplies or improvising electrical connections.

topics.question: How do case airflow and dust affect maintenance decisions?
topics.coverage: Map intake, exhaust, filters and accessibility using manufacturer service guidance; keep electrical cleaning precautions and model-specific disassembly boundaries explicit.

topics.question: What makes a laptop upgrade different from a desktop upgrade?
topics.coverage: Compare soldered parts, service manuals, battery access and chassis clearance for specific models; avoid assuming replaceability from the product family's name.

topics.question: How does a motherboard VRM support a specific CPU under changing load?
topics.coverage: Trace voltage conversion, phases, thermal limits and board power settings on one documented board; do not infer quality or safety from phase count alone.

topics.question: Why can a PC power supply fail during a brief GPU load spike?
topics.coverage: Use a named GPU, PSU and ATX revision to compare sustained draw, excursions, connectors and protection behavior; distinguish shutdown evidence from a wattage-label anecdote.

topics.question: How can Task Manager or another system monitor mislead a performance diagnosis?
topics.coverage: Relate sampling intervals, per-process totals and resource categories to a controlled task; confirm tool definitions before interpreting a high or low percentage.

topics.question: What separates a driver problem from an application or hardware problem?
topics.coverage: Design a reversible diagnosis using event records, version history and a known-good workload; exclude destructive resets as an unexplained first step.

topics.question: Why can startup programs slow access to an otherwise fast PC?
topics.coverage: Measure login-to-ready time and background resource competition in an isolated account; distinguish startup impact labels from observed delay.

topics.question: How should an operating-system reinstall be planned so recovery is possible?
topics.coverage: Inventory backups, application access, licenses, encryption recovery and official installation media; outline decision checkpoints rather than issuing a blanket erase procedure.

topics.question: What did Intel identify in the 13th and 14th generation desktop Vmin instability issue?
topics.coverage: Trace Intel?s dated root-cause statements, affected desktop SKUs, board settings and BIOS microcode versions; distinguish prevention from repair of degraded processors.

topics.question: How can slow Wi-Fi be separated from a slow internet connection?
topics.coverage: Compare local transfer, signal conditions, router placement and wired baselines; state device capabilities and avoid unauthorized network scanning.

topics.question: Why can a USB-C connector support different data, charging and display functions?
topics.coverage: Read host, cable and peripheral specifications together; distinguish connector shape, protocol support and power negotiation using verified documentation.

topics.question: What changes when a display is used for text, color work or fast motion?
topics.coverage: Compare resolution, scaling, refresh behavior, calibration and viewing conditions; avoid reducing suitability to a single panel specification.

topics.question: How can a keyboard, mouse or audio delay be isolated across a setup?
topics.coverage: Separate device, connection, driver and application stages with controlled substitution; report reproducible observations instead of attributing every delay to wireless technology.

topics.question: How should a PC be evaluated for video editing rather than gaming alone?
topics.coverage: Define footage codec, resolution, effects, export path and application version; use representative project tests instead of transferring unrelated benchmark scores.

topics.question: What hardware constraints matter when testing a local language model?
topics.coverage: Compare model size, precision, context memory, runtime support and measured speed; treat compatibility and acceptable responsiveness as different questions.

topics.question: How can a used PC listing be checked for missing or misleading specifications?
topics.coverage: Compare exact component IDs, service history, support status and seller evidence; distinguish disclosed facts from claims that require inspection or return protection.

topics.question: When does a small upgrade have better evidence than replacing an entire system?
topics.coverage: Identify the bottleneck, compatible alternatives, measured workload and total cost; leave prices and personal purchase choices for dated research.

topics.question: When does enabling XMP or EXPO change an actual PC workload?
topics.coverage: Use a specified CPU, motherboard, BIOS and DDR profile; test stability and task time with the profile on and off, separating rated speed from achieved benefit.

categories.title: Accessibility, repair and end of life

topics.question: What should accessible PC setup consider beyond larger text?
topics.coverage: Examine input alternatives, screen-reader support, audio cues and application compatibility with consented user testing; avoid assuming one setting serves all users.

topics.question: How do service documentation and spare-part access change repair feasibility?
topics.coverage: Compare a named machine's procedures, diagnostics, part availability and local repair rules; keep warranty and legal statements jurisdiction-specific.

topics.question: How can a computer be prepared for transfer without exposing the previous owner's data?
topics.coverage: Consult current vendor sanitization guidance for storage type and encryption state; distinguish account sign-out from verified erasure and keep demonstrations on spare media.

topics.question: What happens to a computer after it enters an electronics recycling stream?
topics.coverage: Trace collection, reuse, material recovery and hazardous handling through authorized facilities; do not infer responsible disposal from a recycling logo alone.

topics.question: Why did built-in optical drives disappear from many desktop PCs?
topics.coverage: Compare dated case designs, software distribution, media use and external-drive options; identify markets where discs remain relevant instead of declaring the format dead.

categories.reading_subcategory: Accessibility, repair and end of life

topics.question: What happens before an operating system begins to load?
topics.coverage: Trace firmware initialization, device discovery, boot selection and handoff conceptually; exclude bypassing security controls.

topics.question: How does a computer keep time after it is turned off?
topics.coverage: Compare hardware clocks, firmware settings, network synchronization and operating-system interpretation.

topics.question: What changes when a storage drive reports healthy status but files fail integrity checks?
topics.coverage: Separate hardware indicators, filesystem metadata, memory errors, application writes and backups without diagnosing a real device.

topics.question: Why can a workload fit in RAM yet run slowly because of cache misses or limited memory bandwidth?
topics.coverage: Compare cache hierarchy, locality, working set, access patterns, latency and bandwidth using labeled benign benchmarks; distinguish capacity from the rate and pattern of moving data.

topics.question: What should a firmware-update explanation establish about compatibility and recovery before describing a change?
topics.coverage: Compare exact model, supported version, release notes, configuration retention, recovery documentation and vendor responsibilities; exclude flashing instructions, bypasses or a guarantee that updating fixes an observed fault.

# Computer & PC Channel Master Topic Roadmap (Scratch to Advanced)
**Niche:** 062 Computer & PC (Computing_Software)  
**Channel Language:** English (YouTube)  
**Target Audience:** PC Builders, Hardware Enthusiasts, Overclockers, System Architects, Retro-Computing Geeks (Global)  
**Production Format:** 10-Minute Documentary Explainer Episodes (600s, 75 Fixed 8s Scenes)  
**Execution & Sync Report:** [topics/062_computer_pc/TOPICS_COVERED_REPORT.md](./TOPICS_COVERED_REPORT.md)  

---

## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Computer & PC across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Silicon Architecture, Motherboard Buses & Power Delivery (Scratch / Beginner)** — CPU die layout, PCIe 5.0 lanes, VRM power phases, BIOS/UEFI firmware handoffs, and thermal interface material (TIM) heat transfer.
- **Tier 2: The GPU Revolution, Clock Cycles & Extreme Overclocking (Intermediate)** — Rasterization pipelines vs ray tracing RT cores, CUDA matrix streaming, liquid nitrogen sub-zero benching, and x86 CISC vs ARM RISC microcode.
- **Tier 3: Storage Evolution, Silicon Degradation & Memory Timings (Upper Intermediate)** — Spinning platters to 3D TLC/QLC NAND flash, CAS latency sub-timings, electromigration atomic drift, and transient load line power spikes.
- **Tier 4: Quantum Computing Chips, Neuromorphic Hardware & The Optical Bus (Advanced / Expert)** — Superconducting transmon qubits, dilution refrigerators at 15 millikelvin, memristor neuromorphic processing, and silicon photonics optical interconnects.

---

## 3. Topic Catalog (Scratch to Advanced Curriculum)

### Tier 1: Silicon Architecture & Power Delivery
1. **Why Did Intel Fail to Break 4 GHz for 15 Years? The NetBurst Thermal Wall That Changed PC History**
   - *Question:* Why did Intel promise in 2000 that Pentium 4 would reach 10 GHz, only to hit a catastrophic 130-watt thermal meltdown at 3.8 GHz that forced an entire architectural surrender?
   - *Key Focus:* 31-stage NetBurst execution pipeline, pipeline stall penalties, dynamic power dissipation scaling with frequency cubed (P = C*V^2*f), Israeli design team saving Intel with Core 2 Duo (Conroe).
2. **How a CPU Actually Works: From Quartz Crystals and Clocks to Fetch-Decode-Execute**
   - *Question:* How does an electrical pulse from a vibrating quartz crystal coordinate billions of microscopic silicon transistors through the fetch, decode, execute, and writeback cycle 4 billion times a second?
   - *Key Focus:* Program counter, instruction register and control unit decoding micro-ops, arithmetic logic unit (ALU), L1/L2 cache latency differences, branch prediction.
3. **Motherboard VRMs: The 16-Phase Power Station Keeping Your $600 CPU from Burning**
   - *Question:* How does your motherboard cleanly step down 12 volts from the power supply to an ultra-precise 1.25 volts at 250 amperes without boiling its MOSFETs?
   - *Key Focus:* Buck converter topology, high-side and low-side MOSFETs, ferrite chokes and solid capacitors, pulse-width modulation (PWM) multi-phase switching, Vdroop and Load-Line Calibration (LLC).
4. **Thermal Paste vs Liquid Metal: The Microscopic Battle for Heat Transfer**
   - *Question:* Why does a 0.1-millimeter microscopic air gap trap heat like an oven, and how does gallium-indium liquid metal drop temperatures by 15°C while threatening to short-circuit motherboards?
   - *Key Focus:* Surface roughness and microscopic air voids, thermal conductivity ratings (silicone paste 8 W/mK vs liquid metal 73 W/mK), CPU delidding, gallium galvanic corrosion of aluminum heat sinks.
5. **PCIe Lanes and Chipsets: How Data Moves at 64 GB/s Across the Motherboard**
   - *Question:* What is the difference between lanes wired directly to the CPU and lanes routed through the motherboard chipset, and why do high-end NVMe drives share bandwidth with graphics cards?
   - *Key Focus:* Differential signaling and NRZ vs PAM4 encoding in PCIe 5.0/6.0, direct CPU lanes vs DMI chipset multiplexing, slot bifurcation (x16 to x8/x8), latency implications.
### Tier 2: The GPU Revolution & Overclocking
6. **Ray Tracing vs Rasterization: The 30-Year Battle for Photorealistic Gaming Graphics**
   - *Question:* Why did GPUs fake lighting with rasterized tricks for three decades, and how do dedicated RT cores calculate millions of bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) ray bounces in real time?
   - *Key Focus:* Rasterization polygon projection and depth z-buffering, Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) ray traversal, temporal anti-aliasing and AI denoising (DLSS), rendering physical light physics.
7. **x86 vs ARM: Why Apple Silicon M1 Shocked the Entire PC Industry**
   - *Question:* How did a mobile phone chip architecture humiliate 100-watt desktop Intel and AMD processors while using a tiny fan-less battery chassis?
   - *Key Focus:* CISC variable-length decoding legacy overhead vs RISC fixed-length instructions, massive 8-wide decode engines, Unified Memory Architecture (UMA) on-package bandwidth, memory reordering.
8. **Liquid Nitrogen Overclocking: Breaking 9 GHz at -196°C**
   - *Question:* What happens to silicon transistors when cooled to -196°C with bubbling liquid nitrogen, and why do chips suddenly stop working if they get too cold (the Cold Bug)?
   - *Key Focus:* Carrier mobility increase at sub-zero temperatures, condensation insulation with kneaded eraser putty, the silicon 'Cold Bug' and 'Cold Boot Bug', pushing 2.0+ volts into flagship dies.
9. **Nvidia CUDA: The Secret Software Moat That Created a $3 Trillion AI Monopoly**
   - *Question:* How did Jensen Huang spend hundreds of millions in 2006 to add non-gaming compute logic to every GeForce graphics card, laying the foundation for modern ChatGPT and AI dominance?
   - *Key Focus:* General-Purpose computing on GPUs (GPGPU), SIMT (Single Instruction, Multiple Threads) parallel execution, PyTorch and TensorFlow deep integration, why AMD's ROCm struggled to catch up.
10. **GPU Power Transients: Why 450-Watt Graphics Cards Were Tripping 1,000-Watt Power Supplies**
   - *Question:* Why did modern RTX 30 and 40 series graphics cards shut down high-end power supplies in 10 microseconds, and why did new 12VHPWR power cables melt?
   - *Key Focus:* Microsecond transient spikes exceeding 250% TDP, power supply overcurrent protection (OCP) tripping, ATX 3.0 specification revisions, terminal pin contact resistance in 12VHPWR connectors.

11. **The Evolution of Solid State Drives: From 2.5-Inch SATA to PCIe 5.0 Blowtorches**
   - *Question:* How did storage jump from 500 MB/s SATA bottlenecks to 14,000 MB/s NVMe drives, and why do the newest Gen 5 SSDs require active cooling fans?
   - *Key Focus:* AHCI legacy spinning disk queue limits vs NVMe 64,000 deep parallel queues, 3D charge-trap NAND stacking (232+ layers), controller thermal throttling at 80°C.
12. **SLC, MLC, TLC, and QLC: Why Cheaper SSDs Slow Down to Hard Drive Speeds During Large Transfers**
   - *Question:* How does storing 4 bits of data in a single microscopic floating gate require distinguishing between 16 precise voltage levels, and what happens when the fast pseudo-SLC cache fills up?
   - *Key Focus:* Voltage charge drift, write endurance cycles (TBW) collapsing from 10,000 to 300 cycles, SLC caching buffer tricks, sudden drop to 80 MB/s sustained write speeds.

   - *Key Focus:* Black's Equation for Mean Time to Failure (MTTF), exponential acceleration by temperature and current density (J^2), the danger of manual fixed high Vcore overclocks.

   - *Key Focus:* DRAM capacitor refresh cycles, CAS Latency (tCL) vs turnaround timings (tRFC), refreshing capacitor rows before charge drains, 1% low FPS stabilization in gaming.
